subject: Human Body
title: How Water Is Absorbed
description: A quick, practical guide to How Water Is Absorbed.

hook.text: You drink about 2 liters daily, but your gut processes 9 liters. The extra 7 come from digestive secretions.

buildup.text: The small intestine absorbs most of this water through osmosis as nutrients are pulled across the wall.

discovery.text: Sodium pumps drive water absorption. As sodium moves into cells, water follows by osmotic pressure.

twist.text: Oral rehydration salts exploit this: salt and sugar together pull water in faster than water alone.

climax.text: Water absorption is passive but depends on active sodium transport. Block sodium pumps and diarrhea results.

punchline.text: Salt drives water. That's why rehydration salts work.

quiz.question: What drives most water absorption in the small intestine?
options: Active sodium transport creating osmotic pull
